bullets.title: Iran pause triggers oil selloff, broad risk rally; S&P futures +0.9%
bullets.body: Trump's pause on Iran strikes sent Brent crude down 7%+ to ~$89.58/bbl and WTI to $82.87/bbl, the lowest since July 21. The relief rally lifted S&P 500 futures +0.88% to 7,513, Nasdaq futures higher, and the 10-year yield fell 4bps to 4.63%. European TTF gas fell 6% on the same catalyst.

bullets.title: Peak earnings week: ~$10T market cap reports; FOMC meets Wednesday
bullets.body: Microsoft (~$4.21 EPS, ~$87.4B revenue, ±6% implied move) and Meta (~$7.20 EPS, ~$60.2B revenue) report Wednesday pre-market alongside the Fed rate decision. Amazon, Alphabet, and Apple also report this week. About one-third of the S&P 500 reports in total; 86% of companies reported so far have beaten EPS estimates vs. a 76% ten-year average.

bullets.title: Fed expected to hold; markets price 38% chance of hike — hawkish surprise risk flagged
bullets.body: Consensus expects a fifth consecutive Fed hold at Wednesday's FOMC. However, 22V and Morgan Stanley both flag 38% probability of a hike priced by September, driven by the energy shock and stickier services inflation. JPM notes DM wage growth likely stays above 3% annualized given a steeper post-pandemic Phillips curve, keeping core services inflation above 3% through 2027.

bullets.title: NVDA mulling $250B backstop for OpenAI's Ohio 10GW data center; SK Group $500B+ deal
bullets.body: Nvidia is in advanced talks to provide ~$250B in financing backstop for OpenAI's 10 GW Portsmouth, Ohio data center — the largest DC project ever announced — with total project potentially reaching $600B including chip financing. Separately, NVDA and SK Group announced a $500B+ AI collaboration (SK plans 2 GW data center with Vera Rubin by 2027, scaling to 15 GW by 2035), and AVGO/Samsung announced a $200B+ contract through 2030 for sub-2nm foundry, HBM, and custom silicon.

bullets.title: AI capex dip is a buying opportunity — Morgan Stanley flags unusually attractive entry
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley argues the recent AI infrastructure selloff is primarily technical, not fundamental, and calls it an unusually attractive buying opportunity. Compute demand will materially exceed supply for years constrained by power (38 GW US shortfall through 2028), labor, memory, and grid access. Enterprise token spend is currently under $11/user/month while a typical AI task generates $55 in labor savings on $2-5 token costs. Google Cloud backlog surged from $106B to $514B in a year, underscoring supply scarcity.

bullets.title: Chip stocks surge premarket; semis broadly rebounding on AI capex reaffirmation
bullets.body: SOXX +2.8% in premarket with WDC +4.0%, SNDK +4.1%, MU +3.3%, INTC +2.8%, AMD +2.7%, AVGO +2.1%, NVDA +1.2%. UBS notes GOOGL's capex raise and $700B+ NVDA/AVGO supply chain commitments as sector positives. HDD space flagged by MS as attractive at 7x bull-case CY28 EPS with a 300-400EB annual supply shortfall through CY28 driving pricing toward $25-30/TB.

bullets.title: CXMT IPO surges 472% on Shanghai debut, becomes world's 4th largest DRAM maker
bullets.body: Chinese memory chipmaker CXMT surged ~472% on its first trading day, closing at 49 yuan with a $487B market cap — the largest onshore-listed Chinese company. CXMT is now the 4th largest DRAM maker globally, surpassing Intel in market cap. Reports suggest Shanghai Yuliansheng is manufacturing immersion lithography machines for SMIC/CXMT (~5 this year, ~20 in 2027), raising long-term competitive risk for ASML's China exposure. MATCH Act in Congress could ban ASML immersion litho sales to China.

bullets.title: Macro data solid: Fed regional PMIs in expansion, core capex orders +0.9%, GDP tracking 1.8%
bullets.body: All Fed regional manufacturing indices printed in expansion territory in July, pointing to a robust ISM print (consensus 54.0). Core cap goods (non-defense ex-aircraft) orders rose 0.9% and shipments 1.9% in June, lifting Q2 GDP tracking to 1.8% and equipment investment tracking 8.0% q/q SAAR. Tech orders jumped 3.1% m/m. Texas ISM equivalent rose to 53.3.

bullets.title: S&P earnings breadth strong but price reaction disappointing; quality rotation underway
bullets.body: 86% of reporting S&P 500 companies have beaten EPS estimates vs. a 76% 10-year average, and blended Q2 earnings growth is tracking 37.9% y/y. However, 22V notes the worst downside price skew in 50 quarters with median earnings-day moves down 300bps. Morgan Stanley's Mike Wilson sees a quality rotation accelerating as the early cycle ends — AI adopters expected to outperform both semis and hyperscalers going forward.

bullets.title: Stagflation risk flagged: US tariffs at 10-12.5% on 60 trading partners, pharma at 15%
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley confirms Section 301 tariffs of 10-12.5% met expectations, pushing the effective statutory tariff rate toward 9-10%. CG Asset Management warns the broad tariff scope across 60 partners including the EU and China creates a low-growth, high-inflation environment. Pharmaceutical tariffs modeled at 15%. China is pushing back, calling for removal of 301 measures while signaling openness to talks on mutual respect.

bullets.title: Geopolitical hotspots: Abqaiq oil facility attacked; Iran redirecting ships in Hormuz
bullets.body: Saudi Arabia's Abqaiq facility was set on fire in drone/missile attacks, while Iran redirected multiple vessels through the Strait of Hormuz, characterizing passage as illegal. Despite the US pause on Iran strikes driving the morning risk-on rally, supply risks remain elevated with limited Hormuz transits and Bab-el-Mandeb closures continuing to constrain flows.

bullets.title: XLRE hits highest since spring 2022; CMBS payoff rate improved to 68% in 1H26
bullets.body: The Real Estate ETF (XLRE) closed at its highest level since spring 2022, supported by AI data center tailwinds and solid earnings. US REITs posted $1.3B net inflows in June. CMBS payoff rate improved to 68% in 1H26 with robust 2H26 supply expected; FOMC unlikely to hike at July meeting per Citi real estate team.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler debt spreads widening; 43% of issuance in 10yr+ maturities
bullets.body: Credit spreads on tech/hyperscaler debt have steadily widened, with Oracle 5-year CDS at multi-year highs. Over the past year, 43% of hyperscaler bond issuance carried maturities exceeding 10 years, versus only 24% for M&A deals and 23% for other non-financial issuance — a sign of elevated long-duration financing demand.

bullets.title: SoftBank's $40B OpenAI bridge loan syndicating broadly; 21 new lenders allocate ~$7B
bullets.body: SoftBank's $40B bridge loan for OpenAI has attracted 21 new lenders including First Abu Dhabi Bank and GIC, with approximately $7B allocated to the first tranche. Separately, OpenAI is establishing a new EU HQ in Ireland with 250 jobs, and raised projected compute spending to $750B through 2030 (from $600B).

bullets.title: Anthropic ARR ~$70B; OpenAI 'Presence' enterprise launch threatens SaaS incumbents
bullets.body: Anthropic's ARR is estimated at ~$70B in July, the fastest growth trajectory in tech history. OpenAI launched 'Presence,' an enterprise product for deploying trusted AI agents at the app layer that moves beyond API access, raising disruption concerns for SaaS incumbents. Salesforce won a $1.6B three-year Agentic Enterprise License from the VA, signaling meaningful public-sector AI adoption.

bullets.title: Hedge funds near least-long Mag 7 in 12 months; ~$100B deleveraging easing
bullets.body: Hedge funds are close to their least-long Magnificent 7 positioning over the past 12 months with L/S ratio at the 10th percentile. The ~$100B deleveraging from the AI hardware selloff is easing funding pressures. Retail participation has weakened materially and systematic positioning remains vulnerable to a downside shock. Despite this, Mag 7 stocks all gained in premarket on geopolitical relief: Meta +1.6%, MSFT +1.4%, Alphabet +1.2%, Amazon +1.2%.

bullets.title: Midterm elections <100 days away; Goldman flags flat S&P returns Aug→Election Day historically
bullets.body: US midterm elections are less than 100 days away. Goldman Sachs data shows S&P 500 median return of 0% from start of August through midterm Election Day. Record $225B IPO issuance forecast for 2026 shows late-cycle characteristics historically associated with below-average returns.

bullets.title: BNPL stress rising: 1 in 10 Americans used services last year, one-third missed payments
bullets.body: Buy-now-pay-later usage remains elevated with 1 in 10 Americans using services in the past year, but one-third of BNPL users failed to make their payments — a leading indicator of consumer credit deterioration in the lower-income cohort that Jamie Dimon also flagged as being 'left behind.'

bullets.title: UK CBI retail sales beat sharply; European EPS revision breadth at 4-year highs
bullets.body: UK CBI Retailing Reported Sales came in at -26 in July versus the -47 estimate and -54 prior, suggesting better-than-feared UK consumer conditions. Separately, EPS revision breadth in Europe has risen to a 4-year high, pointing to improving earnings expectations across the continent.

bullets.title: Kazakhstan oil output halves on terminal closure; Russian Black Sea port resumes loading
bullets.body: Kazakhstan's daily oil output halved following a terminal closure, adding to global supply disruptions. Russia's largest oil port in the Black Sea resumed crude loading after a multi-day halt. These supply crosscurrents are playing against the geopolitical de-escalation driving the morning oil selloff.
